A1.justification: Both PDFs describe InvMSAFold, with matching architectures, datasets and extensive retained results. All supplied pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original covariance reconstruction, sequence-diversity, AlphaFold-based refolding and predicted protein-property experiments in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds sampling-time measurements and ProteinMPNN evaluations in Section 4.2 and Appendices A.1 and B.2.

M1.justification: The ESM-IF1 encoder, six-layer transformer decoder, low-rank pairwise and autoregressive models, coupling rescaling and MSA-based training are retained. The fast pseudolikelihood computation already appeared in v1 Appendix A.1; its expanded presentation and the newly measured batching performance do not establish a changed model or algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use CATH protein domains, MMseqs2/UniProt50 MSAs and the same biological evaluation tasks. The 27 appendix PCA domains and protein-property examples are retained. The timing examples evaluate the existing sequence-generation task, without introducing a distinct dataset population or task requirement.

E2.justification: v1's external empirical comparisons use ESM-IF1; ProteinMPNN is only cited. v2 substantially broadens comparison coverage by evaluating ProteinMPNN for covariance reconstruction, native-sequence distance distributions and PCA/KL comparisons across 27 domains (Appendices A.1 and B.2).

E3.justification: v2 adds a targeted timing protocol covering lengths 63, 206 and 437, varying sample counts, batched/unbatched CPU InvMSAFold-AR and GPU ESM-IF1. It also changes the stated Optuna selection criterion from pseudo-likelihood to log-likelihood and identifies the retained v1 Figure 9 refolding domains as intra-cluster. These reported corrections do not establish experimental reruns.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds a focused analysis of runtime scaling with sequence length and sample count, including a batched-versus-unbatched sampling comparison. Existing PCA, distance-controlled refolding and protein-property analyses remain; moving their displays into appendices does not constitute additional analysis.

E5.justification: The refolding error-bar displays and ten-chain MCMC description are retained. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval definitions or significance-testing procedures. ProteinMPNN quartiles extend the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds runtime curves, ProteinMPNN covariance and distance results, and 27 ProteinMPNN PCA/KL entries. For example, its newly reported KL for 1xqiA00 is 6.23, while the retained ESM-IF1, InvMSAFold-PW and InvMSAFold-AR values remain 18.28, 9.19 and 0.27. Existing aggregate covariance/KL results, refolding plots and property plots are retained.

T1.justification: The linear-cost pseudolikelihood derivation moves from v1 Appendix A.1 to v2 Section 2.2.1. Limited formal revisions include changing the quadratic-penalty identity's pair-index range and one-half factors (v1 Equation 9; v2 Equation 7), and explicitly asserting pseudolikelihood consistency. This is not a newly introduced derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims about sequence diversity, structural fidelity and broader predicted biochemical properties remain. v2 adds an explicit orders-of-magnitude sampling-speed advantage over existing methods to the abstract and conclusion, strengthening the specificity of v1's efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds a speculative architecture/training-data explanation for ProteinMPNN's diversity and an untested argument that generated sequences remain detectable through homology-based screening. It also omits v1 Appendix A.2.2's warning that InvMSAFold can leave lower-distance sampling bins empty. The central interpretations of the retained biological results remain stable.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository pointer for training and partial result replication, exact dataset sizes, timing hardware specifications, ProteinMPNN's sampling temperature and an explicit Metropolis-Hastings description. Most existing architectural settings, training hyperparameters and sampling instructions remain. The repository's availability was not checked externally.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Besag (1977) and Vaswani et al. (2017), and expands discussion of ProteinMPNN's architecture and training relative to ESM-IF1. The underlying positioning against inverse-folding and pairwise protein models is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the introduction, methods and experimental prose. It introduces numbered method subsections, separates data splits into their own section, integrates protein-property sampling into Results, moves the low-rank derivation into Methods and relocates detailed training discussion to the appendix. The title, author block and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime Figure 4 and ProteinMPNN Figure 10, expands the appendix PCA displays from three to four comparator panels per domain, and relocates training curves and one refolding figure into the appendix. Multiple captions and the title-page layout are revised; the expanded PCA displays are noticeably more compressed.

improvement.justification: The timing benchmark and actual ProteinMPNN comparisons provide useful evidence absent from v1, while the repository pointer and clearer organization improve usability. These benefits support a limited overall improvement. They are tempered by the removed empty-bin limitation and the new biosecurity detectability assurances, which v2 does not experimentally substantiate.
